Then I’d be hooked: forking out $4.99 and then $9.99 every month, in perpetuity, for the luxury of having Google back up my odds and ends. Granted, Google One might be worth the cost if you want Gemini in your docs and double AI usage without forking out for yet another monthly plan. body: TL;DR Garmin COO Brad Trenkle says MIP displays aren’t disappearing anytime soon because they still offer advantages in battery life and outdoor visibility. Garmin also sees potential for solar-powered OLED watches, although no such product has been announced. A quiet tug-of-war is happening on Garmin wrists. On one side, AMOLED displays are winning hearts with their rich colors, crisp graphics, and gorgeous watch faces. On the other, the less glamorous memory-in-pixel (MIP) screens are still winning endurance contests, especially when the sun is blazing and the nearest charger is miles away. Garmin is increasingly embracing the former, but it isn’t ready to retire the latter. Speaking to TechRadar , Garmin COO Brad Trenkle explained that battery life remains the biggest reason MIP displays still have a place in the company’s smartwatch lineup.

No in-the-wild exploitation has been identified, but the public disclosure could make it easier for threat actors to develop an exploit. Even though Android is a relatively safe operating system, with several security measures in place , threat actors’ ingenuity still keeps finding ways to exploit weaknesses. We recently shared information about malware that can empty your bank accounts in secret , and now, researchers have found a separate Android flaw that could leave your phone outright unusable. Normally, malicious apps need to request permissions and execute code to attack your device. However, researchers at Bitdefender have discovered a new vulnerability dubbed GhostMap that triggers a crash loop simply by installing a specially crafted app.
